'''Peter Di Biasio''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Rogue 39 from London, UK. The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run. [[Trandosite]] interviewed him on 20 July 2000.<ref name="trando-iv5" /> At [[DecipherCon 2000]] he went undefeated and won Day 1 Swiss of the [[2000 Decipher World Championship]].<ref name="tennet">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ DecipherCon 2000: Juz Beer and Cards], Alex "Greedo" Tennet, DeckTech (13 October 2000)</ref>

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables; the tables do not spell out the abbreviation.

== Interviews ==

=== Trandosite, 20 July 2000 ===
Rod Latham interviewed Di Biasio for [[Trandosite]].<ref name="trando-iv5">[http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv5.htm Peter Di Biasio interview], [[Trandosite]] (20 July 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041026204829/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv5.htm Internet Archive]</ref> Trandosite's introduction called him one of the UK's top players. He was a former UK number one and had placed high at the 1999 Antwerp Open.<ref name="trando-iv5" />

* '''Start in the game:''' A friend introduced him to Premiere, and he played from the A New Hope release. His first tournaments were at Gen Con 1997, which led him to events around the UK.<ref name="trando-iv5" />
* '''Highlight:''' The 1999 European Open in Antwerp, which he played with [[Derek Hawkesworth]], Leonard Smith, Ian Ericson, Ian Carter, Matt Allen and Nick Rice.<ref name="trando-iv5" />
* '''Play style:''' He favoured "mains and toys" ground decks, with Darth Vader his favourite card. He blamed his missed finals on poor differential and on playing to crush opponents when he was already winning.<ref name="trando-iv5" />
* '''Practice:''' He playtested regularly with Derek Hawkesworth and Michael Rogers in London.<ref name="trando-iv5" />
* '''Squadron work:''' As Rogue 39 he directed the 2000 Naboo Regionals, which kept him out of that year's qualifying. He planned to play the European Championships.<ref name="trando-iv5" />
